notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/a845d18bda2bfad45f49598842e7070d0904ee9a.png"][/img]Pixel Puzzles World War II, merging history with the definitive jigsaw puzzler on the PC platform.[/p][p]USS Massachusetts (BB-59), a South Dakota–class battleship, saw distinguished service during World War II. Commissioned in 1942, she first entered combat in the Operation Torch landings in North Africa, where she exchanged fire with the French battleship Jean Bart in one of the rare battleship duels of the war. Shortly after, she joined the Pacific Fleet and took part in nearly every major naval campaign, from the Gilberts and Marshalls to the Philippines and Okinawa. Known to her crew as “Big Mamie,” she earned 11 battle stars for her wartime actions, providing heavy gunfire support, protecting carriers, and projecting U.S. naval power across the Pacific.[/p][p]After the war, the USS Massachusetts was decommissioned and placed in reserve, but unlike many of her sister ships, she was preserved from the scrapyard. In 1965, thanks to the efforts of veterans and supporters, she was donated to the people of Massachusetts and permanently berthed at Battleship Cove in Fall River. Today, the battleship serves as a museum ship, open to the public as both a memorial and an educational site. Visitors can explore her decks, learn about her role in the conflict, and experience firsthand the history of one of America’s most storied World War II battleships.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1760951/Pixel_Puzzles_WW2_Jigsaw__Pack_USS_Massachuesetts/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: FREE PUZZLE PACK - D-Day Memorial - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/0e7d3b0ae47a532e155af1b66f0e5890461a0a4b.png[/img]

Today marks the 80th anniversary of the Normandy Landings (June 6, 1944), more commonly known as D-Day. D-Day was a daring invasion plan by the Allied forces as part of a greater plan known as Operation Overlord. Over 150,000 soldiers primarily from the Canada, the United Kingdom, and United States stormed five key beachheads - Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, and Sword. The landings were supported by both naval artillery and strategic deployment of paratroopers behind German lines. The paratroopers were tasked with securing key points such as crossroads and bridges. Deployment of these paratroopers wasn't smooth as many became scattered across Western Europe which created pockets of resistance behind German lines. Nonetheless, the mission was still carried out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/87880050c1939e12e59ca681953ad1c6cfe0be1e.png[/img]

D-Day marked a large turning point in the war as the Allies secured major footholds along the French coast which helped accelerate the liberation of Western Europe. We have added a free pack to the base game showcasing a few memorials and monuments of the past to honor this event.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/4e1a0d7244726124676425b84318fffd1ff8edb6.png[/img]

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/522a142c1bfafacbcf40f24dc204d974171e71d3.png[/img]

USS New Jersey (BB-62) is an Iowa-class battleship that had a storied career that spanned parts of 6 decades. Commissioned in 1943 during World War II, the New Jersey participated in numerous major campaigns in the Pacific Theater, including the Battle of Leyte Gulf and the Battle of Okinawa. Her formidable firepower and robust armor made her a formidable asset in naval engagements, and she provided crucial fire support to ground forces during amphibious assaults. After World War II, the New Jersey was decommissioned in 1948 but was reactivated and modernized in the 1950s to serve during the Korean War and later in the Vietnam War and Lebanese Civil War.

During the Vietnam War, the USS New Jersey served as a floating artillery platform off the coast of Vietnam. Her massive 16-inch guns were used to provide fire support for ground troops and bombard strategic targets inland. 

After her service in Vietnam, the New Jersey was decommissioned for the second time in 1969. However, she was reactivated yet again in the 1980s during the Reagan administration as part of the 600-ship Navy program. She underwent extensive modernization and served during the Lebanese Civil War. The USS New Jersey was finally decommissioned for the last time in 1991 and eventually stricken from the register in 1999. She is currently undergoing repairs in Philadelphia before she returns back to her home in Camden, New Jersey where she serves as a museum ship.

notes.title: Battle of the Bulge - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/5522c2ad9cf898f471973677c53eb1550f6a4a57.png[/img]
The Battle of the Bulge, a pivotal engagement during World War II, unfolded from December 16, 1944, to January 25, 1945. Adolf Hitler aimed to disrupt the Allied supply lines by capturing the Belgian port of Antwerp and splitting their forces. The Germans launched a surprise attack in the densely wooded Ardennes region, catching the Allies off guard. Initially making significant advances, German forces created a salient into Belgium that press referred to as the bulge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/fa191fec5eefc16af0956c077903d0453209fcf4.png[/img]
The Ardennes offensive, however, faced numerous challenges, including unexpected and harsh winter weather that hampered both sides. As the weather cleared, the Allies regrouped and staunchly defended key positions. In addition it allowed the US air support to strike German positions and supplies. General George S. Patton's Third Army played a crucial role in relieving the besieged town of Bastogne, which had become a focal point of the battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/f71147ca2ae73e41874847aa735aeff598045bae.png[/img]
The Battle of the Bulge resulted in significant casualties on both sides, and the Germans could not mount a major offensive for the remainder of the war.

notes.title: FREE DLC - Pearl Harbor - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/e70db6c946ffd2d0b1645a694080ec9ca8e0e6fa.png[/img]
The attack on Pearl Harbor, which occurred on December 7, 1941, was a pivotal event that thrust the United States into World War II. Carried out by the Imperial Japanese Navy, the surprise assault targeted the U.S. Pacific Fleet stationed at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. In a coordinated series of air strikes, Japanese forces inflicted devastating damage on American battleships, cruisers, and aircraft. The attack resulted in the destruction or severe damage of eight battleships, including the USS Arizona, which suffered a catastrophic explosion and sank with the loss of over a thousand lives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/f0d7f7adebc228651e65d1f7602b868800020a3f.png[/img]
The next day President Franklin D. Roosevelt declared war on Japan, marking the beginning of America's active involvement in the global conflict. The aftermath of Pearl Harbor saw a surge in enlistments, industrial production for the war effort, and a commitment to total war. The United States became a key Allied power, contributing significantly to the eventual defeat of Japan and Germany. The attack on Pearl Harbor remains one of the key moments of World War II. While the United States likely would have entered the war at some point, the attack accelerated it and had the American people more supportive of the war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/2338d5f9db805f6dbf042fa48f3de66cbd445b71.png[/img]

notes.title: FREE DLC - Battle Off Samar - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/2e058e5b9bcc0f8e83d214b7df5df17fb66044c0.png[/img]
The Battle off Samar, which took place on October 25, 1944, during the larger Battle of Leyte Gulf, was an engagement in the Pacific theater. The American task force known as "Taffy 3" comprised escort carriers, destroyers, and destroyer escorts, and it found itself facing a vastly superior Japanese fleet, including battleships, cruisers, and destroyers. The Japanese plan was to attack the vulnerable American amphibious landing forces in Leyte Gulf. The American forces, under the courageous leadership of Admiral Clifton Sprague, fought valiantly against overwhelming odds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/315173aba628e27d29d7cba4b96c6fa536150bd7.png[/img]
Two vessels, the USS Johnston (DD-557) and the USS Samuel B. Roberts (DE-413), emerged as the heroes of this battle. The USS Johnston, under the command of Captain Ernest E. Evans, engaged the Japanese fleet with incredible courage and determination, directly challenging the enemy's heavy cruisers and battleships. The Johnston's actions allowed the escort carriers of Taffy 3 to evade destruction and played a critical role in disrupting the Japanese fleet's attack plans. Ultimately, the Johnston was lost in battle, but its fearless engagement is remembered as one of the most heroic episodes of the Pacific War.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/517bff11108595481870d8b14ee6da67ca3d8c35.png[/img]
The USS Samuel B. Roberts, a destroyer escort, also displayed extraordinary bravery during the Battle off Samar. Despite being outgunned and facing imminent danger, the Samuel B. Roberts, under the command of Lieutenant Commander Robert W. Copeland, launched a ferocious attack against the Japanese heavy cruiser Chokai, causing significant damage. Though the Samuel B. Roberts was ultimately lost in battle, its heroic stand, along with the USS Johnston and other vessels of Taffy 3, played a crucial role in disrupting the Japanese attack and securing a victory for the Allies. Despite these actions, Taffy 3 lost 2 escort carriers in the battle, the USS Gambier Bay and USS St. Lo.

notes.title: Battle of Leyte - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/b20032a30b7fe73683ff3cd6c982f191dd78c7ef.png[/img]
The Battle of Leyte was a significant World War II conflict that occurred from October to December 1944 in the Philippines. It marked General Douglas MacArthur's long-awaited return to the Philippines and was a crucial turning point in the Pacific War. The battle was a culmination of amphibious landings and naval engagements, pitting the Allied forces, mainly the United States and Australia, against the Imperial Japanese Army and Navy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/2e213927467a5d122cccfb80d3deb346d51637da.png[/img]
The battle began with a massive amphibious assault on the island of Leyte by the Allied forces. U.S. troops, along with Australian support, landed on the eastern coast of Leyte, facing stiff resistance from Japanese forces entrenched in the area. The battle extended into the seas surrounding Leyte Gulf, where the U.S. Navy and the Imperial Japanese Navy engaged in intense naval conflicts. The Allied forces, particularly the American Third Fleet commanded by Admiral William Halsey, played a vital role in decisively defeating the Japanese fleet in what was the largest naval battle of World War II.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/09d761bd6132406f5ce30043e50278aebb9f9ec4.png[/img]
The Battle of Leyte represented a significant strategic victory for the Allies, ultimately facilitating the reconquest of the Philippines and dealing a severe blow to Japanese naval power. The successful landings and naval engagements in Leyte Gulf demonstrated the Allied forces' ability to execute large-scale amphibious operations and marked the beginning of the end for Japanese control in the Philippines, setting the stage for subsequent operations that led to the liberation of the archipelago and the weakening of Japanese forces in the Pacific.

notes.title: FREE DLC* Soviet invasion of Poland - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/aed9cbb10df0c5774e32dead9bc484f2f7000862.png[/img]
The Soviet invasion of Poland took place from September 17, 1939 to October 6, 1939 as part of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, a secret agreement between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union. Following the German invasion of Poland on September 1, Soviet forces, under the command of Marshal Kliment Voroshilov, crossed into eastern Poland. The invasion further divided Poland, which was already reeling from the German onslaught in the west, ultimately contributing to the country's tragic fate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/e63506172471f192f3ca16b23f04bc7c488f0107.png[/img]
The Soviet invasion aimed to annex territories in eastern Poland, including parts of Ukraine and Belarus, under the pretext of protecting ethnic Ukrainians and Belarusians. The invasion was swift and met with minimal resistance, as the Polish military was overwhelmed by the simultaneous aggression from both Germany and the Soviet Union. The Soviet occupation of eastern Poland brought suffering and repression to the population, as the Soviets imposed their totalitarian regime, arresting and executing perceived political enemies and intellectuals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/c615f930ef573bfabb32a58c69b68797a5fc7582.png[/img]
The consequences of the Soviet invasion of Poland were profound and enduring. The eastern territories of Poland that were annexed by the Soviet Union remained under Soviet control for decades, even after World War II. The invasion further highlighted the vulnerability of smaller nations to the designs of more powerful and expansionist regimes, setting a bleak precedent for the early stages of World War II and the subsequent division of Europe.

notes.title: Battle of Peleliu - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/11dbf29b362e16fe7fec296e071e3baa7aa79a2a.png[/img]
The Battle of Peleliu was a significant confrontation between American and Japanese forces that took place from September 15, 1944 to November 27, 1944 in the Palau Islands. The United States aimed to capture Peleliu, an island with strategic airfields that could be used to support the Allied advance in the Pacific. Under the command of General William H. Rupertus, the U.S. Marine Corps' 1st Marine Division spearheaded the assault. However, the Japanese had heavily fortified the island, prepared to fiercely defend it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/01aee4d2adc8f5307c71c230d7ddd4743dad4a06.png[/img]
The battle commenced with an amphibious assault. The U.S. forces faced intense resistance, as the Japanese were deeply entrenched in elaborate cave systems and fortified positions. The terrain of Peleliu, characterized by sharp ridges and a labyrinth of caves and tunnels, made the battle even more challenging. The fighting was ferocious with both sides suffering heavy casualties. Despite facing a determined enemy and grueling conditions, the U.S. forces eventually gained control of the island, but at a staggering cost in terms of lives lost and wounded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/30fa33c1928f3792912917297c7fb218abfd256c.png[/img]
The Battle of Peleliu was one of the costliest and most contentious battles in the Pacific campaign. The U.S. forces suffered over 10,000 casualties, while the Japanese forces incurred significant losses, with only a few survivors out of their original garrison. The battle highlighted the extreme challenges posed by heavily fortified Pacific islands and the determination of both sides. Despite its strategic value, Peleliu's high casualty rate sparked debate about the necessity of the operation and its impact on subsequent military strategies in the Pacific.

notes.title: The Blitz - OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/5d5f38038813ca2c414ecb12ca61f02f8c0b49d4.png[/img]
The Blitz represents a harrowing chapter in the annals of World War II. This prolonged aerial bombing campaign was orchestrated by Nazi Germany against the United Kingdom, primarily unfolding between September 1940 and May 1941. Its objective was twofold: to demoralize the British population and undermine the country's industrial and infrastructural capabilities. Under the cover of darkness, German Luftwaffe bombers and fighters unleashed relentless air raids, targeting cities across the United Kingdom, with London experiencing some of the most devastating assaults. The Blitz exacted a heavy toll, resulting in widespread destruction, the loss of thousands of civilian lives, and the displacement of countless more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/ea020f0249026aeb9d30942ef5006aea13fdae3f.png[/img]
Despite the widespread devastation, the Blitz showcased the indomitable spirit and resilience of the British people. In the face of adversity, they demonstrated unwavering courage, rallying together under the banner of the "Blitz spirit." This spirit was characterized by unity, determination, and an unyielding resolve to endure the relentless attacks. The Royal Air Force (RAF) played a pivotal role in defending British skies during the Blitz, effectively thwarting the German ambitions of a full-scale invasion. While the Blitz inflicted immense suffering and destruction, it ultimately solidified the British resolve to persevere and triumph over adversity during the tumultuous years of World War II.

notes.title: Welcome to Pixel Puzzles World War II
notes.notes:
With this product, we delve into a multitude of battles, events, and the military-industrial complex of that era. Every pack comes with a brief historical overview, while the "Specials" pack offers intriguing images accompanied by historical insights. We invite you to relish this journey into the past, as you explore the significant and lesser-known events that played pivotal roles in shaping World War II.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/76bc77945ce82adde35eb3a20bbcd07f7c4a4f37.png[/img]
The Invasion of Poland in September 1939 stands as a pivotal moment in world history, marking the beginning of one of the deadliest conflicts ever witnessed - World War II. This invasion was a meticulously planned military campaign orchestrated by Nazi Germany, led by Adolf Hitler, and the Soviet Union, under the leadership of Joseph Stalin. The aggression against Poland was a blatant violation of numerous international agreements and treaties, including the Treaty of Versailles, which had ended World War I.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/c12fb39e834ae44865d641dfd0f4be8b2c986876.png[/img]
The invasion itself unfolded with astonishing speed and ferocity. The German military employed their innovative blitzkrieg tactics, characterized by coordinated movements of tanks, infantry, and air support, to overwhelm the Polish defenses. Poland, caught between two formidable adversaries, faced a devastating assault from both east and west. The Polish armed forces fought valiantly, but the overwhelming firepower and superior strategies of the invaders proved too much to bear. Within weeks, Poland was overrun, its cities bombed, and its people subjected to the horrors of war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/07b018df93a8379d2f9398930bfdbf0438196086.png[/img]
The aftermath of the invasion was catastrophic. Poland was divided between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union along the agreed-upon demarcation line in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. This division resulted in the suffering of the Polish population, as both occupiers pursued their own agendas and subjected the Polish people to harsh repression, forced labor, and mass deportations. Meanwhile, the invasion of Poland prompted a swift response from Western democracies. Britain and France, honoring their commitments to support Poland in the event of an attack, declared war on Germany on September 3, 1939. This formal declaration marked the escalation of the conflict into World War II, a global conflagration that would last for six years and encompass nearly every corner of the globe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44542431/1f2195f16d7bbcc608cfb904bdaf64870a685ca4.png[/img]
World War II was a harrowing period in human history, characterized by widespread destruction, the Holocaust, and the loss of an estimated 70-85 million lives. The Invasion of Poland remains a stark reminder of the devastating consequences of unchecked aggression and the tragic toll that warfare can exact on nations and individuals alike. It serves as a somber lesson in the importance of diplomacy, international cooperation, and the preservation of peace to prevent such catastrophic conflicts in the future.
